theorems.name: Triangle No-Arbitrage Determines the Third Rate
theorems.description: For positive exchange rates S_AB and S_BC (S_XY = units of Y per unit of X), exactly one rate S_CA leaves the three frictionless conversion trades A→B, B→C, C→A without arbitrage (no real combination whose net holding is non-negative in every currency and positive in one), namely S_CA = 1/(S_AB·S_BC). No-arbitrage is the multi-state FTAP's notion with the currencies as coordinates; reverse trades are at the reciprocal rate, and bid–ask spreads and transaction costs are not modelled.

theorems.name: Put-Call Parity from No-Arbitrage
theorems.description: Under a positive linear pricing functional (state prices q summing to the discount factor and pricing the spot), the call minus put portfolio is worth S0 - K*DF. First-principles parity, no distributional hypothesis.

theorem putCall_parity_from_no_arbitrage_thm
    {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (q : ι → ℝ) (S : ι → ℝ)
    (DF S₀ K : ℝ)

    finite-state call-price functional `K ↦ Σᵢ qᵢ · max(Sᵢ − K, 0)` is convex in

theorems.name: Cone-Separation Root (Convex-Duality Unification)
theorems.description: A closed convex cone in (ι → ℝ) disjoint from the standard simplex admits a strictly-positive functional that is ≤ 0 on the cone. This single geometric Hahn–Banach fact is the shared root of three apparently separate pillars: the FTAP (attainable-gains cone ⟹ the EMM), the coherent-risk representation (acceptance cone ⟹ representing density), and superhedging (super-replication cone ⟹ the price bound).

code.lean:
import MathFin.Pricing.Duality.ConvexDuality

/-- **Cone-separation root — the shared kernel of the convex-duality unification.**
    A closed convex cone `C ⊆ (ι → ℝ)` containing no probability vector (no nonnegative `v` with
    `∑ i, v i = 1`, i.e. disjoint from the standard simplex) admits a
    strictly-positive functional `q` that is `≤ 0` on `C`. One Hahn–Banach fact, three
    instances: the FTAP (apply to the attainable-gains cone — the separating `q` is the
    equivalent martingale measure), the coherent-risk representation (apply to the
    acceptance cone — `q` is a representing density), and superhedging (apply to the
    super-replication cone — `q` prices the bound). Re-exports
    `MathFin.exists_pos_separating_of_cone_disjoint_simplex`. -/
theorem convex_duality_root {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (C : Set (ι → ℝ)) (hCconv : Convex ℝ C) (hCclosed : IsClosed C)
    (hCcone : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ C → ∀ ⦃c : ℝ⦄, 0 ≤ c → c • x ∈ C)
    (hdisj : ∀ v : ι → ℝ, (∀ i, 0 ≤ v i) → ∑ i, v i = 1 → v ∉ C) :
    ∃ q : ι → ℝ, (∀ i, 0 < q i) ∧ ∀ v ∈ C, ∑ i, q i * v i ≤ 0 :=
  MathFin.exists_pos_separating_of_cone_disjoint_simplex C hCconv hCclosed hCcone hdisj

theorems.name: Fundamental Superhedging Bound
theorems.description: In a finite-state one-period market with excess-return matrix z, every martingale probability vector q (q ≥ 0, Σq = 1, every asset's excess return q-fair), in particular every equivalent martingale measure, prices a claim at most any of its super-replication costs: Σ_n q n Y n ≤ x whenever x plus some portfolio dominates Y in every state. theorems.name: Second FTAP on a Finite Probability Space: Complete if and only if the Equivalent Martingale Measure is Unique
theorems.description: On a finite probability space with a full-support real-world measure P, a filtration whose horizon σ-algebra 𝓕 T is the whole σ-algebra, an adapted scalar discounted price S over a finite horizon T, and no arbitrage: the market is complete (every bounded claim is, P-a.s., an initial wealth plus the gains Σ φ_{t+1}(S_{t+1} − S_t) of a bounded predictable strategy φ) if and only if there is exactly one equivalent martingale measure. Complete ⇒ unique: replicate the indicator of an event; every equivalent martingale measure gives it the initial wealth as probability. Unique ⇒ complete: if the replicable claims (constants plus the span of the one-period increment-indicators) are a proper subspace, a nonzero functional vanishing on it perturbs the strictly positive weights of the equivalent martingale measure into a second one.

theorems.name: d-Asset One-Period FTAP (Esscher EMM, finite-dimensional market)
theorems.description: On an arbitrary probability space, for a ℝᵈ-valued discounted excess return Y, no arbitrage ⟺ there is an equivalent martingale measure Q ~ P with Y integrable and E_Q[Y] = 0 ∈ ℝᵈ — with no non-redundancy hypothesis. The backward direction is an explicit logistic-tilt construction (the softplus analogue of the Esscher measure, not the Esscher measure itself): minimise the smooth convex potential θ ↦ E[log(1 + exp⟪θ,Y⟫)]. The potential is constant along the gains kernel N = {θ : ⟪θ,Y⟫ = 0 a.e.} and coercive on its orthogonal complement Nᗮ, so a minimiser on Nᗮ is automatically global (redundant directions absorbed); its first-order condition E[Y·σ⟪θ₀,Y⟫] = 0 (σ logistic) yields a strictly-positive bounded density.

The MathFin theorem is stated for a discounted excess return valued in any finite-dimensional real inner-product space F (the ℝᵈ market is F = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)). Redundant assets are thereby absorbed (no quotient by the gains kernel or measurable selection needed). No Hahn–Banach, no L⁰-cone closedness, no measurable selection. theorems.name: Change of Numéraire (Price Invariance)
theorems.description: Given a pricing measure Q for the money-market numéraire B and a second strictly-positive numéraire N, the numéraire measure Q^N (Radon–Nikodym density dQ^N/dQ = (N_T·B₀)/(N₀·B_T)) reprices every terminal claim X consistently: N₀·E^{Q^N}[X/N_T] = B₀·E^Q[X/B_T]. This is the abstract change-of-numéraire theorem — the shared backbone of the library's concrete numéraire changes (the Black–Scholes stock numéraire, the exchange-option second-asset numéraire, the Garman forward/annuity normal form).

theorems.name: Replication Determines the Pricing Measure (Abstract Second FTAP, Easy Direction)
theorems.description: Let Gains be a class of terminal gains and Q1, Q2 probability measures dominated by P under which every gain is integrable with mean zero (gains-neutral). If the indicator of every event of a sigma-algebra G is P-a.s. equal to an initial wealth x plus a gain from Gains (the market is complete for G), then Q1 and Q2 agree on G. The abstract argument behind 'complete implies the pricing measure is unique': replicate the indicator, and every gains-neutral measure gives the event the initial wealth. theorems.name: Piecewise-Linear Arbitrage-Free Interpolation of a Quoted Call-Price Smile
theorems.description: Reduced core: Kahalé (Risk 17(5), 2004, 102–106) poses and solves the problem of building, from finitely many market call-price quotes that are already free of static arbitrage, a continuum interpolant that is itself free of static arbitrage everywhere between them — via a C² scheme whose pieces have Black–Scholes form plus an affine term, obtained from two nested non-linear minimisations. This entry proves the existence half for the simplest such scheme, piecewise-linear interpolation: a discrete dataset with increasing strikes, non-increasing prices (no vertical-spread arbitrage) and non-decreasing secant slopes (no butterfly arbitrage) extends to a function that is convex and non-increasing on the whole quoted strike range, and that matches the data exactly at every knot and along every linear segment. Kahalé's own C² construction is not formalised here: a correct implementation of his scheme would additionally land in that smoothness class through his two-stage minimisation (whose convergence Le Floc'h, arXiv:2004.08650, notes is not proven). No extrapolation beyond the quoted strike range is derived either, and the price bounds of IsNormalizedCallPrice (intrinsic value below, forward above) are neither assumed on the quotes nor derived for the interpolant.

import MathFin.Models.ModelFree.CallPriceInterpolation

open MathFin Set

/-- **Piecewise-linear arbitrage-free interpolation of a quoted call-price smile.** A finite
dataset of `n + 1` arbitrage-free call-price quotes (increasing strikes, non-increasing prices,
non-decreasing secant slopes) admits a piecewise-linear interpolant that is itself convex and
non-increasing on the whole quoted strike range, and matches the quoted data exactly, both at
the knots and along every linear segment. Re-exports `MathFin.convexOn_piecewiseLinear`,
`MathFin.antitoneOn_piecewiseLinear`, `MathFin.piecewiseLinear_eq_knot` and
`MathFin.piecewiseLinear_eq_segment`. -/
theorem piecewise_linear_arbitrage_free_interpolation (K C : ℕ → ℝ) {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (hq : IsArbitrageFreeQuotes K C n) :
    ConvexOn ℝ (Icc (K 0) (K n)) (piecewiseLinear K C n) ∧
      AntitoneOn (piecewiseLinear K C n) (Icc (K 0) (K n)) ∧
      (∀ i ≤ n, piecewiseLinear K C n (K i) = C i) ∧
      (∀ i, i + 1 ≤ n → ∀ x ∈ Icc (K i) (K (i + 1)),
        piecewiseLinear K C n x = C i + (C (i + 1) - C i) / (K (i + 1) - K i) * (x - K i)) :=
  ⟨convexOn_piecewiseLinear K C hn hq, antitoneOn_piecewiseLinear K C hn hq,
    fun _i hi ↦ piecewiseLinear_eq_knot K C hn hq hi,
    fun _i hi _x hx ↦ piecewiseLinear_eq_segment K C hn hq hi hx⟩

theorems.name: Arbitrage-Free Call Quotes Are the Prices of a Market
theorems.description: Finitely many call-price quotes C_i at increasing strikes 0 = K_0 < ... < K_n that are free of static arbitrage (non-increasing prices, non-decreasing secant slopes), start at the forward 1 at strike 0, end at the worthless call C_n = 0 and lie above intrinsic value are the call prices, at the quoted strikes and maturity one, of a market with unit numeraire, a nonnegative asset of forward one and a pricing measure. Scope: existence of a market reproducing the quotes at maturity one; no uniqueness, no smoothness of the call price function, and no calendar-spread or multi-maturity content.
